upstream.description: Living Domain×Form matrix of every repo I've forked, with one-shot LLM abstraction + use cases. Self-updating via Actions, viewable on Pages.

classification.analysis: fork-atlas is a self-updating, server-less catalog of every GitHub repo the owner has forked, classified into a Domain x Form matrix with a one-shot write-once LLM classification pass and keyword-tagged use cases. It runs entirely on GitHub Actions (discovery/build with only the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN) and GitHub Pages (a vanilla-JS static site with no build step), and includes an assistant page that answers 'which of my forks fit project X' via a two-stage BM25-then-LLM retrieval pipeline against Ollama, an Anthropic API key, or no LLM at all, all provider credentials kept client-side. It is aimed at a solo builder who wants a searchable, governed memory of hundreds of forked repositories without a database or backend server.

use_cases.title: Classify hundreds of forked GitHub repos into a searchable domain/form taxonomy automatically
Ask a static assistant page which of my forks best fit a new project brief
Run repo discovery and classification with no server, database, or stored secrets
Retrieve candidate repos locally via Ollama before falling back to a cloud LLM
